record.context_brief: Temporal chromatic number of the Minkowski plane
record.original_question: Determine the chromatic number χτ(R1,1) of the 2-dimensional Minkowski space-time R1,1, where χτ(R1,1) is the smallest number of colors in a coloring of R1,1 such that no two points A and B with temporal distance τ(A, B) = 1 receive the same color. In particular, is χτ(R1,1) finite?

evidence.quote: • χτ (R1,n), the smallest number of colors in a coloring of R1,n in which no two points A and B with τ (A, B) = 1 have the same color;
First open problem. What is the value of χτ (R1,1)? Is it finite?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{R}^{1,1}$ denote the two-dimensional Minkowski space-time, i.e., $\mathbb{R}^2$ equipped with the (indefinite) bilinear form of signature $(1,1)$. For two points $A=(t_A,x_A)$ and $B=(t_B,x_B)$ in $\mathbb{R}^{1,1}$, define their temporal distance by
$$\tau(A,B)=\sqrt{\,(t_A-t_B)^2-(x_A-x_B)^2\,}\qquad\text{when }(t_A-t_B)^2\ge (x_A-x_B)^2,$$
and leave $\tau(A,B)$ undefined (or set to $0$) otherwise; thus $\tau(A,B)=1$ means $A$ and $B$ are time-like separated with unit Minkowski proper-time interval.

Define the temporal chromatic number $\chi_\tau(\mathbb{R}^{1,1})$ to be the smallest cardinality of a set of colors that admits a coloring $c:\mathbb{R}^{1,1}\to C$ such that whenever $\tau(A,B)=1$, one has $c(A)\ne c(B)$.

Determine the value of $\chi_\tau(\mathbb{R}^{1,1})$. In particular, decide whether $\chi_\tau(\mathbb{R}^{1,1})$ is finite.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as the first open problem in a recent survey on chromatic numbers of space-times. Web searches related to chromatic numbers in Minkowski-type spaces (work of Raigorodskii and others) do not return any source claiming a determination of $\chi_\tau(\mathbb{R}^{1,1})$ or even a proof of its finiteness, so the problem appears still open.
